summary: Bald Butte, 15 miles NW of Burns, Oregon: 1931 first lookout, 1959 41-foot R-6 timber tower; a 2007 report says it burned, a 2018 visit found it standing and abandoned.

facts.design: R-6 wooden flattop cab on a 41-foot treated timber tower
facts.status_note: Sources disagree: a 2007 FFLA Oregon report lists it as lost and burnt to the ground, but a May 2018 visit found the tower still standing.

access.note: A Forest Service fence surrounds the base (2018 visit). The sources describe no public climbing and no rental.

visit.trail_note: 2018 visit: a short dirt spur road from Road 41, blocked by a fallen tree about half a mile up

events.note: First lookout: a wood tower completed August 12, 1931 by George Roba and Ira Swift. Forest Lookouts quotes 42 ft; the register describes a 45-foot pole tower
Frank Merritt occupied the tower for the balance of the 1931 season
The first lookout was replaced by the current 41-foot R-6 timber tower
Registered July 16, 2002 as US 425, OR 50; nominated by Howard Verschoor
Listed as lost in 2007 (1959-2007) and described as burnt to the ground. A 2018 visit found the tower standing, so this is disputed
May 25, 2018 visit found the tower standing, abandoned, in bad shape, with pieces scattered below and a Forest Service fence at the base

corrections.why: The register and Forest Lookouts describe the current tower as 41 feet tall (about 12.5 m). The record's 2.4 m does not match any source read.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register and Forest Lookouts date the first lookout to 1931; a 2018 visit gives 1935 for a 45-foot pole tower with a ground cabin. The current tower's 1959 date is the same in every source that gives one.

sources.title: Bald Butte – Every Lookout in Oregon

notes_for_editor: Status is disputed and needs a human decision before the record changes. The FFLA Oregon 2007 report lists Bald Butte as lost in 2007 and burnt to the ground; the May 2018 visit describes the tower as still standing, abandoned and in bad shape; firelookout.com (undated) says condemned and severely vandalized. The record's 'standing' is left unchanged. Height: record 2.4 m is wrong; the register and Forest Lookouts say 41 feet, so a correction to 12.5 m is proposed. The first tower's height also disagrees (register 45 ft pole tower; 1931 Ochoconian quote 42 ft wood tower). Staffing: register says 'staffed as needed' (undated); 2018 visit says not staffed in decades. Elevation: record 1788.3 m matches the register's 5,867 ft; firelookout.com gives 5,920 ft, not reconciled. Forest designation: the register and Forest Lookouts say Ochoco National Forest; the coordinates are in Harney County, which I did not check against forest boundaries. Sources are thin and two are undated blog or personal pages. Page reads used: 7 (one over the 6 guideline, within the 8 cap). No WebSearch used.
